items.prompt: Two C++ workers write the same ordinary int without ordering, then main joins both. What is the key issue?

options.text: Final joins automatically repair earlier worker races
options.why: They order worker completion with main, not the unsynchronized conflicting worker actions.

options.text: The only permitted final values are 1 and 2
options.why: Undefined behavior is not limited to a toy schedule table.

options.text: The workers have a data race; later joins do not repair it
options.why: At least one conflicting action is non-atomic and neither is ordered before the other.

options.text: A passing run proves no race exists
options.why: Dynamic outcomes do not establish all required ordering.

items.explanation: Identify conflicting unordered worker accesses, not merely whether main waits before printing.
